To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
antiarrhythmic treatment in patients with CHD does not reduce mortality.

(1) prophylactic antiarrythmic drug treatment in patients with CHD and left ventricular dysfunction does not reduce mortality and (2) in patients with CHFD and atrial fibrillation, restoration of sinus rhythm does not reduce mortality.

antiarrythmic drugs have not shown any effect on mortality, but βblockers have; the effect of βblocker treatment on mortality seems to be due to other effects than antiarrhythmic effects and the effect is independent of the antiarrhythic effect; atrial fibrillation is an important cause of mortality in CHF; the present treatment strategy for atrial fibrillation in patients with CHFs may be questioned.

antiarrhythmic treatment with amiodarone and βblockers in CHF patients does not reduce mortality.
